title: silent-metering-delta-from-archived-namespace-proxies
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Summary: Several customers reported discrepancies between console billing and provider invoices after archival and API key rotations for nested sub-organizations. Initial tracing shows a small but persistent amount of ingress events attributed to archived namespaces via long-lived proxy tokens. This ticket covers investigation, short-term mitigation, reconciliation/backfill, and a protocol-level fix to prevent recurrence.

Scope: impacts multi-tenant attribution at org/project level when a sub-organization is archived or promoted and an API key rotation occurs on parent service-accounts. Affects rate limiting counters, usage metering, and billing aggregation for a subset of customers in NA and EU regions.

Objective: isolate writes from archived namespaces, reconcile misattributed usage, harden token->tenant resolution path, and add observability to detect reoccurrence.
root_cause_summary: Race in the ingress claim-resolution path: when a sub-organization is archived we relied on cache TTLs and eventual propagation to invalidate proxy entries. During an API key rotation the proxy chain re-emitted requests using an ephemeral delegating token that resolved to a fallback tenant mapping (root org) for a window of ~15-90 minutes, causing silent metering deltas. In addition, archived namespaces were not tagged with a durable tombstone in the metering pipeline, so downstream aggregators accepted and counted the events without rejecting or attributing them to a separate 'archived' bucket.
proposed_fix_summary: 1) Enforce authoritative token->tenant mapping at the gateway using the central tenancy service (no cache fallback when a namespace is in 'archived' or 'disabled' state). 2) Write a tombstone marker to the metering pipeline for archived namespaces; reject or tag subsequent writes. 3) Update rate-limiter keys to include tenancy version id to avoid cross-tenant counter reuse during rotations. 4) Run a reconciliation backfill job to identify the last 30 days of affected events and reattribute to correct projects or offset invoices where appropriate.
implementation_steps: Gateway change: consult tenancy service on every new token handshake; return HTTP 401 for tokens bound to archived namespaces (feature-flagged).
Metering pipeline: accept 'tombstone' tag and route counts to a staging bucket instead of live billing until reconciliation completes.
Rate limiter: add tenancy_version to composite key and deploy a rolling upgrade across regions.
Backfill: build event reattribution job with safeties and sampling; run in dry-run then apply phase with manual approval.
Add alerting: metric for unknown-tenant writes and tombstone-write attempts with paging to on-call.
Docs: update runbook and dev guide for namespace archival and key rotation best practices.
acceptance_criteria: No live writes attributed to archived namespaces during a 48h shadow period (observed via shadow metrics).
Backfill job produces a verified reattribution report with <=0.1% false-positive rate on sampling checks.
Rate limiter composite keys show no counter collisions across tenant-version rollouts in staged regions.
Consequence-free rollback path exists and is tested in staging.
qa_plan: 1) Unit + integration tests for tenancy handshake behavior. 2) End-to-end staging test: create org->suborg, archive suborg, rotate keys, assert gateway rejects or tags writes. 3) Run backfill dry-run on a 7-day sample and validate reattribution against original invoices. 4) Load test rate limiter with simulated rotations to ensure counters isolate correctly.
rollback_plan: Revert gateway handshake change via feature flag; switch metering pipeline back to previous behavior; abort backfill if reattribution thresholds fail. Primary rollback path validated in canary region.
estimated_cost_and_risk: Medium engineering effort with potential customer-facing billing adjustments; risk mitigated by shadowing and manual approval for backfill. Legal/finance will be informed before applying reattribution adjustments.
